newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES, INDIANS BEGIN ROAD TO POSSIBLE SERIES REMATCH.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES, INDIANS BEGIN ROAD TO POSSIBLE SERIES REMATCH.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves and Cleveland Indians begin the road back to a possible World Series rematch as Major League Baseball launches the playoff season on Tuesday.

The powerful Indians travel to Baltimore to play the homer-happy Orioles and kick off the divisional playoffs on Tuesday. The World Series champion Braves host the Los Angeles Dodgers in their best-of-five series starting Wednesday.

The other opening-round tests have the re-tooled New York Yankees taking on playoff newcomers Texas Rangers, and the fast-closing San Diego Padres squaring off against the St Louis Cardinals in the National League.

Atlanta and Cleveland were once again the best teams in their respective leagues this season, as the pitching-rich Braves led the National League with 96 wins, while Cleveland won a major-league best 99 games.
But the best-of-five format allows little margin for mistake and could spring surprises ahead of the best-of-seven league championship series that set the World Series teams.
Cleveland fell to Atlanta in six games in last year's Fall Classic, but return to the playoffs with better balance in their attack and a hunger to claim the Series crown.

The Tribe shipped off slow-running sluggers Carlos Baerga, Eddie Murray and Paul Sorrento, and replaced them with Kevin Seitzer, Julio Franco and Jose Vizcaino -- moves that improved team speed and put more runners on base.

Seitzer (.326 avg.) hits behind leadoff man extraordinaire Kenny Lofton (.317, 75 steals) to set the table for Jim Thome (.309, 38 homers, 116 RBI), Albert Belle (.311, 48 homers, 148 RBI) and Manny Ramirez (.309, 33 homers, 112 RBI).
A deep bullpen backs up Charles Nagy (17-5, 3.41 ERA), Orel Hershiser (15-9, 4.24) and Jack McDowell (13-9, 5.11).
The Orioles set a major league record for home runs in a season with 257, including 50 from their own extraordinary leadoff hitter, Brady Anderson.
But Baltimore's pitching is suspect and ace Mike Mussina (19-11, 4.81) has been struggling. David Wells (11-14, 5.14) starts against Nagy in the opener.

The Yankees, beaten by Seattle in last year's Divisional Series, added a National League flavor to their roster after taking on new manager Joe Torre and general manager Bob Watson, fresh from recent tours of duty in the other league.

New York mixed in Mario Duncan (second base), Joe Girardi (catcher), Darryl Strawberry (DH) and back-up third baseman Charlie Hayes to a lineup featuring Bernie Williams, Tino Martinez, Paul O'Neill and rookie shortstop Derek Jeter.

New York hopes starters David Cone (7-2, 2.88), Andy Pettitte (21-8, 3.87) and Jimmy Key (12-11, 4.68) can hand over a lead to star relievers Mariano Rivera (8-3, 2.09) and John Wetteland (43 saves, 2.83).

Texas, appearing in their first playoff series, rely on the booming bats of right fielder Juan Gonzalez (.314, 47 homers 144 RBI) and third baseman Dean Palmer (38 homers, 107 RBI) and a dangerous lineup full of .300 hitters.
Texas' pitching is shaky after ace Ken Hill (16-10) and Darren Oliver (14-6), who starts the opener against Cone.
In the National League, the Braves will once again send out the best starting pitching in baseball as they try to reach their fourth World Series of the last five played.

John Smoltz (24-8, 2.94) has taken over as top gun from Greg Maddux (15-11, 2.72) and Tom Glavine (15-10, 2.98) on a blue ribbon starting staff that is backed up by reliever Mark Wohlers, who saved a club record 39 games this season.
Chipper Jones (.311, 30 homers and 110 RBI) heads a lineup that also features Fred McGriff (28 homers, 107 RBI) and Ryan Klesko (34 homers, 93 RBI).
It will be strength against strength when the Braves meet the Dodgers, who also rely on stellar pitching.

Starters Hideo Nomo (16-11, 3.19), Ismael Valdes (15-7, 3.32) and Ramon Martinez (15-6, 3.42) make do on the run support they receive from the dangerous middle of the Dodgers' order -- Mike Piazza (.336, 36 homers, 105 RBI), Eric Karros (34 homers, 111 RBI) and Raul Mondesi (24 homers, 88 RBI).

San Diego swept three from the Dodgers in Los Angeles last weekend to avert a series with the Braves. Instead, the Padres draw the surprising St Louis Cardinals, whose team has been revamped since the hiring of former Oakland Athletics manager Tony LaRussa.

The Padres have a potent attack spearheaded by spectacular third baseman Ken Caminiti (.326, 40 homers, 130 RBI), Tony Gwynn (.353 for his seventh batting title), and Steve Finley (.298, 30 homers, 95 RBI).

San Diego's pitching, however, is thin after ace starter Joey Hamilton (15-9, 4.17) and Fernando Valenzuela (13-8, 3.62), and pitching is the strong suit for St Louis, which features former A's hurler Todd Stottlemyre (14-11, 3.87), Andy Benes (18-10, 3.83) and Donovan Osborne (13-9, 3.53).
